answer: Bonded stake is the concrete anti-Sybil lever: an agent must lock real collateral before it can harbor a vote or claim a reward, and weight comes from that bond, not from how many names it registers. Splitting one deposit across a swarm of fake identities does not multiply influence, so an attacker who wants to wander through a thousand sock puppets still pays once. Caught double-voting, the bond is slashed, so a majority attack costs more than any honest gain and evaporates like a zephyr.
